how_it_wins:
Your commander does his best work without ever showing up. Eminence functions from the command zone, so every other Vampire spell you cast mints a free 1/1 from turn one — stack 002 put that on the record, and stack 009 leaned on it again. Here is the trap, and it is the one that actually costs games: waiting for Edgar. His median cast is turn six and the simulation only lands him by then in 52.3% of games, so deploy into an empty board and let the table price you as a creature deck.

The kill is what happens when those free bodies land. Purphoros, God of the Forge, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Corpse Knight each turn a creature entering into life gone from every seat at once — no attack, no blockers, no evasion. Stack 009 counts the whole sequence: one two-mana Vampire, one Anointed Procession, three of those payoffs on the table, nine triggers, twelve damage to each opponent. You have a converter in hand in 52.5% of games at a mean turn of 3.28, and a converter plus a multiplier in 40.2%. Build every turn toward that pairing.

Combat is your other kill and it shows up sooner than anything else you own — a lord or anthem in 83.2% of games, mean turn 2.60. Stack 003 prices what that buys: seven attacking Vampires under Sanctum Seeker with Bloodletter of Aclazotz out is fourteen out of every opponent at declare-attackers, before a single blocker exists. Attack early and attack wide; the drain happens whether or not the creatures get through.

You also own a deterministic table-kill, twice over, and you should hold it lightly. Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or with Sanguine Bond is a free, unbounded loop, both verified (stacks 004 and 006) — and you draw a complete pair in 4.6% of games. That is a ticket you happen to be holding, not a plan. Every one of those three cards pays rent as a body or a drain the other nineteen games in twenty, so present the loop when a window opens and never slow the board down to protect it.

combo_lines.002: Start with the clause that keeps this arithmetic honest. When two replacement effects want the same event, CR 616.1 hands the choice to “the affected player” — that is you — and CR 614.5 gives each effect exactly one opportunity at the event or anything replacing it. Anointed Procession and Mondrak, Glory Dominus both want your single eminence token; each gets one bite. The holding: one becomes two becomes four, and the order you choose cannot change the answer. Two riders worth carrying to a table — eminence works from the command zone because it names the zone it works in (CR 113.6b), and tokens are created rather than cast, so they never trigger eminence a second time.
combo_lines.003: One word does all the work here, and the word is “instead.” Bloodletter of Aclazotz says an opponent who would lose life during your turn loses twice that much instead; CR 614.1a makes that a replacement effect, and CR 614.5 gives it one application per loss event rather than one per turn. Declaring seven Vampire attackers is seven separate Sanctum Seeker triggers (CR 603.2c), so the doubling applies seven times, taking 1 to 2 each time. The holding: fourteen out of every opponent at declare-attackers, before a blocker exists. Your own gain of 1 per trigger is never doubled — the clause speaks only to an opponent's loss.
combo_lines.004: The whole case turns on a parenthesis. Bloodthirsty Conqueror triggers whenever an opponent loses life, and the italic “(Damage causes loss of life.)” beneath it is reminder text — CR 207.2a, a summary of a rule, not a requirement that the loss arrive as damage. So Vito's targeted life loss feeds it and the handshake closes. The holding: a deterministic table-kill for zero mana, retargetable on every iteration because CR 115.1d picks targets fresh as each trigger goes on the stack, and shortcut-legal so you never have to count it aloud. The cost is on the record too — both halves are creatures, and every iteration hands priority to a table that may be holding removal.
combo_lines.006: Read the two triggers side by side: Sanguine Bond's is Vito's, word for word — “Whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life.” Everything settled about the Conqueror half carries over untouched, so the finding worth naming is exposure. Bond is an enchantment, which means this pairing offers exactly one creature for a removal spell to answer instead of two. The holding: the same free, deterministic table-kill with one fewer target — and the chain survives a mid-loop death, because the killing loss triggers Conqueror before state-based actions (CR 704.5a) remove the player from the game.
combo_lines.007: Take this one as the warning label it is. Throne of the God-Pharaoh fires at the beginning of your end step, and the end step is still your turn, so Bloodletter's doubling applies — separately to each opponent's loss. Then count what is tapped rather than what is frightening: the seven attackers are tapped, and Bloodletter itself stayed home untapped, so it does not count itself. Fourteen out of each seat. The holding, stated the way the record states it: this is verified reach and a refuted table-kill. An opponent at 15 survives at exactly 1, nobody's opponents have all left, and play continues in your end step.
combo_lines.008: The question of law is a counting question, and CR 603.2c answers it: an ability “can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.” Four tokens arriving together is one event with four occurrences, not one entry — so Purphoros triggers four times, then a fifth time when the Vampire spell itself resolves and enters. The holding: five triggers at 2 apiece, 10 damage to every opponent, out of a single two-mana cast with no combat step anywhere in it. And the ordering is yours to waste: had an opponent fallen to an earlier trigger, the remaining ones would still have resolved against everybody else.
combo_lines.009: CR 113.6 is the sentence to sit with — abilities of an object function “while that object is on the battlefield.” On the battlefield, not as a creature. Devotion to red is three here, so Purphoros is an enchantment and no body at all, and its trigger fires regardless, because a permanent's abilities work from the battlefield whatever its card type. With that settled the count is mechanical: two tokens arrive as one event with two occurrences, Cordial Vampire arrives as a third event, and CR 603.6a checks every permanent against each of them. The holding: nine triggers off one two-mana Vampire, twelve damage to each opponent, exactly lethal into a pod at twelve with zero margin. One trigger fewer and all three seats live.

card_roles.Edgar Markov: The engine, and it runs from the command zone: every other Vampire spell you cast mints a free 1/1, taxed by nothing and answerable by nobody. Cast him when you want the alpha strike — his attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control — not because you feel you ought to.
card_roles.Anointed Procession: Doubles every token event you generate, which means it doubles eminence, Mavren Fein, Legion's Landing and Charismatic Conqueror all at once. Four mana that turns a two-drop into a lethal turn under the damage payoffs (stack 009).
card_roles.Mondrak, Glory Dominus: A second doubler on a 4/4, and it stacks with the first because each replacement effect gets exactly one bite at the event (stack 002). The indestructible counter is genuine sweeper insurance — pay it on a turn you have bodies to spare.
card_roles.Elspeth, Storm Slayer: A third token doubler that also makes a token every turn and destroys a creature with mana value 3 or greater. Her 0 is usually the better button: a counter on every creature plus flying is an attack the table did not price.
card_roles.Purphoros, God of the Forge: Two damage to each opponent for every other creature that enters — the largest converter in the deck. He is usually not a creature at your devotion, which costs you a body and costs the trigger nothing (stack 009).
card_roles.Impact Tremors: One damage to each opponent per creature entering, for two mana. Cheap enough to land before the doublers do, which is exactly when you want the conversion layer online.
card_roles.Warleader's Call: Impact Tremors with an anthem attached: the +1/+1 makes your tokens 2/2 while the trigger drains all three seats. It is the payoff that improves both of your kills at once.
card_roles.Corpse Knight: A fourth converter for two mana, and the only one that causes life loss rather than damage. Not a Vampire, so casting it makes no eminence token — cast it anyway, and early.
card_roles.Cathars' Crusade: Every creature entering puts a +1/+1 counter on your whole board, so one doubled eminence trigger grows the team several times over. Follow it with Abzan Falconer and those counters become flying.
card_roles.Charismatic Conqueror: Taxes every untapped creature or artifact your opponents play: they tap it, or you get a lifelinking Vampire token. Two mana that makes tokens on other people's turns, which the converters are delighted to see.
card_roles.Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fo: A one-mana Vampire token that flips into a land the moment you attack with three creatures. Play it on turn one; the back face is a mana source and a token factory nobody can two-for-one you on.
card_roles.Mavren Fein, Dusk Apostle: Attack with any nontoken Vampire and he makes a lifelinking token — doubled by your doublers, converted by your converters. He rewards the attack you were making regardless.
card_roles.Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage: A 2/2 flier every turn with no mana attached, and once you control five Vampires he flips into a lord that keeps making them. One of the few token engines that never asks for a card from your hand.
card_roles.Ocelot Pride: A one-drop that makes a Cat at every end step you gained life, and with the city's blessing copies every token that entered this turn. Not a Vampire, so no eminence trigger — the copies more than cover it.
card_roles.Preacher of the Schism: Deathtouch on a 2/4 that either makes a token or draws a card every time it attacks, depending on who is at the top. Attack the life leader; the token is worth more to you than the card.
card_roles.Elenda, the Dusk Rose: Grows on every creature death and cashes out into that many lifelinking Vampire tokens when she dies. Let her die to the sweeper — that is the best version of this card, not a loss.
card_roles.Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet: Exiles the nontoken creatures your opponents lose and hands you a 2/2 Zombie for each, so a wipe you cast leaves you a board. His lifelink also switches on Vito and Sanguine Bond.
card_roles.Legion Lieutenant: Two mana, an eminence token, and +1/+1 on every other Vampire — the cheapest anthem here. Play it early: the tokens it pumps have not been made yet.
card_roles.Stromkirk Captain: +1/+1 and first strike for every other Vampire, which turns a row of 1/1 tokens into blockers nobody wants to trade with. The first strike is the half people forget to fear.
card_roles.Captivating Vampire: A lord that steals a creature whenever you can tap five Vampires, and tokens tap perfectly well. Take the blocker before the alpha strike, not after it.
card_roles.Patchwork Banner: Name Vampire: an anthem that also taps for any colour, which is the fixing this three-colour base genuinely wants. It is a lord you can cast off an awkward mana draw.
card_roles.Shared Animosity: Every attacking Vampire gets +1/+0 for each other attacker sharing its type — quadratic, not additive. Hold it until the board is wide, then watch ten attackers become lethal out of nowhere.
card_roles.Abzan Falconer: Every creature with a +1/+1 counter gains flying, and after one Edgar attack or one Cathars' Crusade trigger that is your whole board. Not a Vampire, but it is the card that ends games the blockers were winning.
card_roles.Vampire Socialite: Menace on a two-drop, and once an opponent has lost life this turn every other Vampire enters with an extra +1/+1 counter — including all four tokens from a doubled eminence trigger (stack 002). Drain first, then deploy.
card_roles.Cordial Vampire: Counters on every Vampire you control each time any creature dies, yours or theirs. It turns a board wipe into a growth spurt for whatever walks out the other side.
card_roles.Drana, Liberator of Malakir: Flying first strike that puts a counter on every attacking creature when she connects — counters Abzan Falconer then reads as flying. Send her at the open seat.
card_roles.Knight of the Ebon Legion: A one-mana threat with a pump that makes it a 4/5 deathtouch, and it grows itself whenever a player lost 4 or more life this turn, which your converters do routinely. Excellent on turn one, still excellent on turn ten.
card_roles.Vampire of the Dire Moon: One mana, deathtouch, lifelink: the cheapest eminence trigger in the deck and a blocker nobody attacks into. The lifelink also feeds Vito.
card_roles.Bloodletter of Aclazotz: Doubles each opponent's life loss on your turn — Sanctum Seeker's drain, Corpse Knight, Throne of the God-Pharaoh (stacks 003 and 007). Your own gain is never doubled; the clause speaks only to an opponent's loss.
card_roles.Sanctum Seeker: Every attacking Vampire drains each opponent for 1 and gains you 1, so seven attackers is seven triggers (stack 003). Blockers do not stop a single point of it.
card_roles.Throne of the God-Pharaoh: Two mana: each opponent loses life equal to your tapped creatures at your end step, so a wide attack drains twice over. Stack 007 prices it honestly — that is reach, not a kill.
card_roles.Bloodthirsty Conqueror: A 5/5 flying deathtouch body that gains you life whenever an opponent loses any, which with Vito or Sanguine Bond is a free deterministic table-kill (stacks 004 and 006). Even alone it turns every drain into a lifegain engine.
card_roles.Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose: Every point of life you gain becomes a point an opponent loses, and with Bloodthirsty Conqueror that is a verified infinite (stack 004). Do not forget his lifelink activation — on a wide board it is a real button.
card_roles.Sanguine Bond: Vito's trigger on an enchantment, which is one fewer creature for a removal spell to answer (stack 006). Five mana is the price of being harder to break.
card_roles.Twilight Prophet: Once you control ten permanents — which happens quickly here — every upkeep reveals a card and drains each opponent for its mana value while you gain it. A 2/4 flier that wins the long games unassisted.
card_roles.Bontu's Monument: Black creature spells cost {1} less and every creature spell you cast drains each opponent for 1. The discount is the point: it is what lets you cast two Vampires in a turn, which is two eminence triggers.
card_roles.Herald's Horn: Name Vampire: every Vampire spell costs {1} less and your upkeep digs for one off the top. This deck wins by casting two spells a turn, and this is the card that pays for the second.
card_roles.Henrika Domnathi // Henrika, Infernal Se: Three modes, one per turn: an edict everybody pays, a card, or a flip into a lifelink deathtouch flier that pumps the team. Take the edict when someone is protecting a single creature.
card_roles.Strefan, Maurer Progenitor: Blood tokens for every player who lost life this turn — which your converters guarantee — and sacrificing two puts a Vampire from hand onto the battlefield attacking. Cheating a five-drop into combat is the mode that ends games.
card_roles.Caretaker's Talent: Draws a card the first time tokens enter each turn, which here is every turn. Level it with spare mana: level 3 makes every creature token +2/+2 permanently.
card_roles.Welcoming Vampire: A card every turn a small creature enters, and every token you make is power 2 or less. Three mana that refills your hand off the plan you were already running.
card_roles.Night's Whisper: Two cards for two mana and two life. Cast it on a turn with nothing better to do; the life is cheap at this speed.
card_roles.Demonic Tutor: Any card, no restrictions. Point it at whichever converter closes from the board you actually have, not at the flashiest card in the list.
card_roles.Vampiric Tutor: Instant speed, puts the card on top, costs you a turn of draw. Cast it on the end step before your turn so the card is in hand when you untap.
card_roles.Diabolic Intent: Demonic Tutor for two mana with a creature as the additional cost — and you make 1/1 tokens for free. Sacrifice a token, never a lord.
card_roles.Teferi's Protection: Phases out your entire board and makes your life total untouchable until your next turn. Three mana that answers a wrath, a combo kill and a lethal swing with the same card.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free while you control your commander: indestructible for the whole team. Hold it on every turn Edgar is on the battlefield, because that is precisely the turn a sweeper costs you the game.
card_roles.Akroma's Will: With your commander out you take both modes: flying, vigilance and double strike alongside lifelink, indestructible and protection from every colour. On a wide board it is not a trick, it is the kill.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Four damage to a player, indestructible for your permanents, or double strike on one creature. Two mana with three answers earns the slot even in the games you only ever pick the middle one.
card_roles.Deflecting Swat: Free with a commander, and it changes targets rather than countering — point their removal at their own creature. Keep it up on the turn you go for a kill.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for {1} to equip. Equip on the turn Edgar attacks, so the counter trigger lands and he cannot be answered in response.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: One mana, exiles the creature, and the life you hand over barely matters at your speed. Save it for the thing that genuinely blanks your attack.
card_roles.Path to Exile: Exile a creature for one mana and give them a basic. It is the answer you can hold up on turn one and still deploy on the same turn.
card_roles.Despark: Exiles any permanent with mana value 4 or greater at instant speed for two. Your answer to the enchantment or artifact that stops the entire plan.
card_roles.Anguished Unmaking: Exiles any nonland permanent at instant speed for three life and no mana-value floor. That makes it the broader half of the deck's noncreature answers — hold it for the cheap enchantment Despark cannot touch.
card_roles.Winds of Abandon: One-sided by design: overload for six and every creature you do not control is exiled while yours stand untouched. A wrath that leaves you holding the alpha strike.
card_roles.Olivia's Wrath: Every non-Vampire creature shrinks by your Vampire count, and every token you make is a Vampire. On a wide board this is a one-sided wipe for five mana.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: Pay the life, choose the number, kill exactly what needs killing — and it answers indestructible. Expensive in life, which is the fee for the only sweeper here that scales.
card_roles.Cemetery Gatekeeper: Exiles a card from a graveyard on entry, then pings whoever plays a card sharing that type. Choose the type deliberately: exiling a land taxes the whole table every turn.
card_roles.Forerunner of the Legion: Searches up any Vampire and puts it on top, then pumps a creature every time another Vampire enters. It is a body, an eminence trigger and the most reliable way to find Bloodthirsty Conqueror.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Two colourless on turn one or two. It fixes nothing and deploys a three-drop a turn early, which in this deck is an entire extra eminence trigger.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any colour in your identity for two mana — the cleanest fixing you own. Cast it on turn two whenever your untapped colours do not line up with your hand.
card_roles.Talisman of Indulgence: Black or red for one damage, colourless for free. The rock that fixes your heaviest colour and your lightest one on the same card.
card_roles.Ancient Tomb: Two colourless for two life — the fastest land in the deck, and your speed is worth the life. It pays for a three-drop on turn two.
card_roles.Command Tower: All three of your colours, untapped, at no cost at all. Lead with it on any turn that does not demand a specific colour later.
card_roles.Cavern of Souls: Name Vampire and your Vampire spells stop being counterable, on a land that arrives untapped. Read the restriction: that coloured mana casts creature spells only, so pay for Castle Locthwain and Bloodline Keeper from somewhere else.
card_roles.Mana Confluence: Any colour, one life a turn. In a base where black wants three pips and white wants two, that is the cheapest fixing at the table.
card_roles.Reflecting Pool: Any colour a land you control could produce, so it is a second Command Tower the moment a real land is beside it. On turn one alone it does nothing.
card_roles.Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth: Every land you control becomes a Swamp, which repairs the deck's shortest colour with one card. Sequence it early whenever the hand is black-hungry.
card_roles.Nomad Outpost: All three colours, always tapped. Lead with it on a turn you are casting nothing, never on the turn you want a one-drop.
card_roles.Savai Triome: Three colours tapped, and it cycles for three when you are flooded. The tapped turn is the fee for never being colour-screwed.
card_roles.Blood Crypt: Black and red untapped for 2 life. Pay it: black pips arrive from turn one here, and a tapped land on turn two costs you a Vampire.
card_roles.Godless Shrine: Your two heaviest colours on one untapped land for 2 life. This is the shock you should almost always pay for.
card_roles.Sacred Foundry: Red and white for 2 life. Red is the colour you need least and latest, so this is the shock you are most often content to take tapped.
card_roles.Battlefield Forge: Red or white for a damage, colourless for free. Painlands are the untapped fixing this curve wants on turns one and two.
card_roles.Caves of Koilos: White or black for a damage, always untapped. The pain version of the pair you want most often.
card_roles.Sulfurous Springs: Black or red for a damage. Reach for it on the turn you need a third black pip and cannot afford to wait.
card_roles.Silent Clearing: White or black for a life, and it cashes itself in for a card once you are flooded. Untapped fixing that stops being a dead draw late.
card_roles.Sunbaked Canyon: Red or white for a life, and it draws a card when you no longer need lands. The red source you least mind spending.
card_roles.Blazemire Verge: Black or red untapped as long as you already control a Swamp or a Mountain. Fine from turn two onward, awkward as your opener.
card_roles.Bleachbone Verge: Black or white once you control a Plains or a Swamp. Your best turn-two untapped land and a blank turn-one one.
card_roles.Concealed Courtyard: White and black untapped while you control two or fewer other lands — a fastland that gets worse the longer it sits in your hand. Play it early or accept the tapped turn.
card_roles.Haunted Ridge: Black or red untapped once two other lands are down. The mirror of the fastland: clumsy early, clean afterwards.
card_roles.Shattered Sanctum: White or black untapped from your third land onward. Your best mid-game dual for the two colours that matter most.
card_roles.Sundown Pass: Red or white untapped after two other lands. The least painful red source once the game is properly underway.
card_roles.Luxury Suite: Black and red untapped in any pod of two or more opponents, which is every game you play. Treat it as a plain dual and stop thinking about it.
card_roles.Spectator Seating: Red and white, untapped at a multiplayer table. Free fixing for the colour you need least often.
card_roles.Vault of Champions: White and black untapped at a multiplayer table — the pair this deck asks for most, with no life paid for it.
card_roles.Castle Locthwain: Black, untapped once you control a Swamp, plus a repeatable draw that costs life equal to your hand size. Cash it in when you are empty, never while holding four cards.
card_roles.Minas Tirith: White, untapped when you control a legendary creature, and it draws a card in any turn you attacked with two creatures. Your board makes that condition trivial.
card_roles.Takenuma, Abandoned Mire: A black source that channels from your hand to return a creature, costing {1} less for each legendary creature you control. A land that is never a dead card.
card_roles.Bloodstained Mire: Fetches a Swamp or a Mountain, Blood Crypt included, for a life. Crack it on their end step so the shuffle happens before your draw.
card_roles.Marsh Flats: Fetches Godless Shrine, a Plains or a Swamp — the fetch that finds both of your heaviest colours.
card_roles.Prismatic Vista: Fetches any basic for a life, which here means a Swamp nine times out of ten. Fix first and worry about the life afterwards.
card_roles.Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid: A tapped black source that can instead be cast as a sorcery to sacrifice a token for two cards, with the land still playable later from exile. Two cards for a 1/1 you made for free is a trade you should take.
card_roles.Plains: Your only white basic, and the card every fetch and every Winds of Abandon overload promises. Remember it exists before you fetch a Swamp on autopilot.
card_roles.Swamp: Four copies of your heaviest colour and the default target for every fetch. Black carries the most pips in the deck — take the basic over the clever land when the turn is tight.

mulligan:
You are not fighting your own list for an opener. 81.8% of first sevens clear the goldfish's keep rule and mean mulligans run 0.215, so set a high bar and take the free look when a hand misses it.

The bar is simple: two to four lands and two Vampires you can cast by turn three. There are eight one-drops and seventeen two-drops to find, and each of those casts is a body plus an eminence token before it does anything else. A hand like that is already a clock.

Ship the all-payoff seven. Sanguine Bond, Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Cathars' Crusade in the same hand does nothing until turn five and then asks the table's permission. Ship zero- and one-land hands, ship six-land hands, and ship anything whose cheapest spell costs four.

Do not dig for a named card, not even the good ones. A lord or anthem finds you in 83.2% of games at a mean turn of 2.60 and a multiplier in 78.2% at 2.68; the converters — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight — are the thinner leg at 52.5%. Keep a curve that can use one the moment it lands instead of mulliganing toward it.

Two details decide the close keeps. Fifteen of the 37 lands can enter tapped, but only Nomad Outpost, Savai Triome and Midgar, City of Mako do it unconditionally — Cavern of Souls and Command Tower both arrive untapped, so a two-lander holding either is a genuine turn-one keep. And Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Indulgence, Herald's Horn, Bontu's Monument or Patchwork Banner turns a marginal seven into a good one; ramp or fixing shows up in 67.7% of games at a mean turn of 2.98.

Never keep a hand for Edgar. His median cast is turn six, eminence is running from the command zone the entire time, and a seven built around your slowest card is a seven built around nothing. Keep the hand that casts a two-drop on turn two and let him arrive when he arrives.
upgrades:
Price everything here against one rate. A card that turns a creature entering the battlefield into life gone from every seat is in your hand in 52.5% of games, 42.3% of them by turn six. Pair one with a multiplier and you are at 40.2%, mean turn 4.53. The intuition underneath those numbers: the bodies are never the shortage — a multiplier or extra token-maker turns up 78.2% of the time at a mean turn of 2.68 — and roughly three games in five reach turn six with the conversion layer still in the library.

That is why the cheapest thing this deck can buy is another rung on a ladder it already owns. The corpus arithmetic is blunt about it: five copies of an effect is 31% of opening sevens, seven copies is 41%, ten is 54% (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors). One more converter moves the number that decides the game further than any single more powerful card does, because it moves the number you see every game rather than the ceiling you see occasionally.

There is a second figure that prices a search effect exactly. The surviving infinite assembles in 4.6% of games on its own and 25.0% once unrestricted tutors count as wildcards. Twenty points is what a tutor is worth here, and it is the same twenty points that argue against buying a third copy of a two-card kill you see one game in twenty. Tutor the irreplaceable, stack the classes you want every game.

One thin place is worth a slot rather than a shrug: an answer to a noncreature permanent is in hand in 30.8% of games, off two cards, at a mean turn of 3.59. Against three opponents that is the axis that binds, and it is cheaper to widen than any ceiling on the board.

And one number to stop worrying about while you shop. The bracket floor is 4, set by four Game Changers — Ancient Tomb, Demonic Tutor, Teferi's Protection, Vampiric Tutor — rather than by combo content. Nothing on this list moves the tier, so the tier should not shape the list. Buy rate: another converter, another source of entries, or the mana to deploy two of them in one turn.
mana_base:
Thirty-seven lands across 34 entries, and the figure to sit with first is 15 — the number that can enter tapped. That is 41% of the base against the one-in-three budget the deck builder allows itself, which sounds worse than it plays: only three of them enter tapped no matter what. The rest are shocks, verges, fastlands and battle lands that come in untapped once you meet their condition. The tempo shows up in the simulation — land drops hit 99.9% on turn two and 92.5% on turn three, with mean available mana of 2.141 and 3.168 on those turns.

The interesting disagreement is between pip share and source share, and it is almost entirely black. Black carries 49.4% of the deck's coloured pips on 41.8% of its coloured sources — 38 pips across 28 cards, up to three at once, wanted from turn one. Red runs the other way at 14.3% of pips on 25.5% of sources, and it never asks for more than one at a time, never before turn two. White nearly agrees with itself: 36.4% against 32.7%. You are best supported in the colour you need least.

On-curve probability prices that skew exactly. From lands alone, white arrives 84.9% of the time and red 76.2%; black arrives 66.7%. Your tightest leg is your heaviest colour, and that single comparison is the whole shape of this mana base.

Five rocks buy a real slice of it back. Arcane Signet, Patchwork Banner, Talisman of Indulgence, Sol Ring and the flipped Legion's Landing lift black from 23 land sources to 26 total and 66.7% to 74.2%, white to 89.5%, red to 83.1%. Sol Ring adds speed rather than colour; Patchwork Banner is the standout, because it is an anthem that taps for any colour. The two cost reducers, Herald's Horn and Bontu's Monument, lower the bill instead of raising the sources — on a curve this cheap that is the same purchase.

About the 90% yardstick: it asks for 36 black sources against 22 red and 22 white. Thirty-six black sources inside a 37-land deck is arithmetic that does not exist, and the audit says so itself — a yardstick, not a possibility. Read the gap as posture. Sequence black first, keep the untapped black-white lands for one-drop starts, and let Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth do its trick: with it down, every land you control is a Swamp. One restriction to hold in mind while you do it — Cavern of Souls names a creature type and its coloured mana casts creature spells only, so it cannot pay for Castle Locthwain's draw, Bloodline Keeper's flip or Captivating Vampire's steal. Its colourless mode still can.
threat_assessment:
The table reads Edgar Markov at seat assignment, and you should let it. Eminence works from the command zone, so a Vampire cast on turn two is a body whether or not you ever pay six mana for him. The goldfish measures 0.91 bodies by turn two, 1.75 by turn three and 4.12 by turn six. "I haven't done anything yet" is not a sentence available to you.

So stop spending your deflection budget on anonymity. It cannot buy that (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection). What it can buy is the order you deploy three specific cards in, and that ordering is worth more than any bluff you could tell.

Here is the flip point, and it is exact. You go from a creature deck to the archenemy the first time a token entering deals damage at all three seats. Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros each do that. Before that trigger you are a fair board. After it, everyone is on your clock and no combat step is required.

The flip is measured, not felt. A token-to-damage payoff is drawn in 43.2% of games at a mean turn of 3.45. Paired with a multiplier, 33.4%, mean turn 4.66. Stack 008 verifies the ceiling: with Anointed Procession and Mondrak, Glory Dominus down, one two-mana Vampire is five Purphoros triggers and 10 damage to each opponent.

So sequence payoffs early and multipliers late. Impact Tremors on turn two with one body is one damage and reads as durdle; nobody spends removal on it. Anointed Procession is three mana that visibly does nothing. Elspeth, Storm Slayer is a five-mana planeswalker and gets attacked on sight, so she is the last piece down, never the first.

Now the good news, and say it out loud at the table. A creature sweeper is the wrong answer to you. Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Caretaker's Talent, Patchwork Banner, Legion's Landing and Elspeth all live through one. Purphoros is indestructible, and while your devotion to red is under five he is not even a creature.

Eminence rebuilds at one token per Vampire cast, with no card spent and no commander tax. That makes the wrath in someone's hand a bad trade against you and a fine one against the seat to your left. Pointing that out is free, and it is true, which is the only kind of table talk that keeps working.

Your actual exposure is the enchantment layer. Track which seat holds broad exile or artifact-and-enchantment removal, and treat that player as the one who can turn the machine off.

Bloodthirsty Conqueror is the card to stay quiet about, and the reason is not that it wins. It is that it wins so rarely. The pairing with Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond is a verified deterministic table-kill (stacks 004 and 006), and it is drawn in 4.8% of games, 2.6% by turn six, 24.0% counting the three tutors as wildcards. That is a lottery ticket riding along with a real plan. Never hold the board back to protect it.

Deploy that package by how each card looks. Vito is a three-mana Vampire and a lord target, so cast it on curve and it tells nobody anything. Conqueror is a 5/5 flying deathtouch body that pays full rent, so cast it as a body whenever you do not hold the other half. Sanguine Bond is five mana with no body and no creature type, and it is the one card in the deck that announces itself.

Stacks 004 and 006 both name the honest cost: instant-speed creature removal in any iteration's priority window breaks the loop. Count the table's open mana before you present it (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). If a seat has two untapped and a reputation for holding, cast the enchantment half and pass.

Then take the label, on the turn the arithmetic is already there. Two boards qualify. A payoff plus a multiplier with three mana untapped and a Vampire in hand, where every cheap cast is now a burn spell aimed at the whole table. Or Edgar on the battlefield, median turn six and 52.2% by turn six, handing the board first strike, haste and a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire at declare, with Akroma's Will available to add flying and double strike, or indestructible and protection from each colour, or both.

When you take it, take it insured. A protection piece is held in 68.0% of games and 56.6% by turn six, and four of the nine are board-wide. Teferi's Protection answers the sweeper and the counterattack with one card. Commit on the turn you can cover, and the table gets exactly one window to stop you — usually holding the wrong card for the job.
matchups:
VS SWEEPER CONTROL: The wrath is a worse card against you than it is against anyone else at the table, and you should build the whole matchup on that. The machine is not made of creatures — Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Caretaker's Talent, Patchwork Banner, Legion's Landing and Elspeth, Storm Slayer all survive, Purphoros is indestructible, and eminence rebuilds at one token per Vampire cast with nothing spent. So commit exactly the width that converts now and keep the next multiplier in hand: "commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further" and "buy resilience instead of restraint" (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). With a payoff down you do not need seven bodies to matter — stack 008 puts one two-mana Vampire at 10 damage to each opponent through two doublers. Rebuild worst-first afterwards. Assume the white or blue seat sitting on four or more untapped mana with no play is representing the sweeper, and time your commitment to a protection piece: held in 68.0% of games, 56.6% by turn six, four of nine board-wide, with Teferi's Protection covering the wrath and the swing-back together. Impact Tremors is the card that flips this matchup — two mana, invisible, and it turns every rebuild into damage the sweeper cannot undo.

VS STAX AND TAX: Structurally your best matchup, and the reason is a rules detail worth knowing cold. Eminence is a triggered ability that functions from the command zone, not a cast, so a Sphere effect taxes the Vampire spell and never touches the token it makes. The curve cooperates: 9 one-drops and 17 two-drops out of 63 spells. You are the beatdown here by force, racing the lock's completion, so recount your hand under the tax and name your outs early — the piece that beats you is the one that stops tokens entering or taxes creature spells, not the flashiest lock piece (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Herald's Horn rebates {1} on every Vampire creature spell and Patchwork Banner taps for any colour while pumping the type, which is a real counter-tax on a deck built to cast two spells a turn. Edgar himself is the first thing a tax prices out at six mana, and you do not need him: median cast turn six, 52.2% by turn six, and the token engine has been running since turn one regardless. Leave him zoned longest in this matchup, aim Despark at the tax rather than the trophy, and remember Ancient Tomb is two mana under any Sphere.

VS AGGRO AND CREATURE MIRRORS: Re-ask the role and take the other seat (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Against a faster board you are the control, and this deck can do that without changing a single card — lifelink tokens from Charismatic Conqueror, Legion's Landing, Mavren Fein and Preacher of the Schism, deathtouch from Preacher and Vampire of the Dire Moon and the Conqueror, first strike from Edgar, Cemetery Gatekeeper and everything Stromkirk Captain touches. A wide board turns their small creatures into dead cards without you drawing anything, and that virtual advantage triples against three opponents (strategy:card-advantage.virtual). Charismatic Conqueror is the card that flips it: every artifact or creature entering untapped under any opponent either comes in tapped or hands you a lifelink Vampire, and with a payoff down that token deals damage to all three seats on their turn. Olivia's Wrath is your asymmetric answer — each non-Vampire creature gets -X/-X for the Vampires you control, and the goldfish has you at 4.12 bodies by turn six. Toxic Deluge kills your own board, so hold it only for a board you genuinely cannot race. Spend life freely where it buys tempo — Ancient Tomb, Mana Confluence, Caves of Koilos and four fetches are all charging you — but track each opponent's clock separately, because 40 life attacked from three directions is not 40 life.

VS COMBO: You are the clock and you are fast enough to be one. The lord package assembles at a mean turn of 2.58 and the token-to-damage payoff at 3.45, which is ahead of most combo decks' assembly. Present the plan that survives being answered: an interrupted multiplier costs one card, an interrupted alpha strike costs the board, so lead with entry damage rather than a swing (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). Held answers rot against combo, and the last profitable moment is now — spend Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile and Despark on the piece that ends the game rather than saving them for the piece that looks scary (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). This is the matchup where casting Edgar early for reasons other than combat is right: he switches on Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat for free. Do not steer toward the Conqueror loop here — it is drawn in 4.8% of games, and both stacks 004 and 006 break it to one instant-speed removal spell at any iteration. Race, and let the loop happen to you if it happens at all.

VS GRAVEYARD HATE: This one is close to free, and you should encourage it. There is no graveyard plan to attack — the kills are token entries, attack triggers and a lifegain loop, and every payoff is a permanent on the battlefield. A Rest in Peace effect costs the reanimator seat their deck and costs you one trigger on Cemetery Gatekeeper, whose enters ability needs a card in a graveyard to exile before its damage trigger can ever check. Say yes to that trade every time and help the hate resolve. Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet is your own flip card against a recursion deck: opponents' nontoken creatures get exiled instead of dying and you get a 2/2 Zombie for each, which is hate stapled to a body a lord already pumps. Cemetery Gatekeeper is the second, and it is a first-striking Vampire on the way to being incidental hate.
